D.t: Cinde Warmington trails by 8.4 and wins 9% of simulations. Closing it takes about 28,983 voters switching sides, or 57,967 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +16.5 and R +0.5. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +9.0. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at R +3.7; your worst is National Public Affairs at R +15.1. 7 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Grafton, a projected net 5,834 votes; Cheshire, a projected net 4,344 votes; Strafford, a projected net 944 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Hillsborough, R +10.8, 28.3% of the vote; Merrimack, R +6.6, 11.3% of the vote; Strafford, D +1.5, 9.3% of the vote; Cheshire, D +11.5, 5.5% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cinde Warmington runs furthest behind in Belknap, Carroll, Hillsborough. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 94% of voters, 43 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.70 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 46 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 47 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Cinde Warmington: Immigration voters 12 to 85, New and irregular voters 36 to 60, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 38 to 58. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$400K cash against $2.6M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
